#### 1. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.790)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:18060)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in ARX (null) —DISRUPTS→ ARX (HGNC:18060); ARX (HGNC:18060) —DECREASES→ Neuronal development and migration (GO:0022008); Neuronal development and migration (GO:0022008) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Neuronal development and migration (GO:0022008) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function variants in ARX disrupt neuronal development and migration, leading to intellectual disability and seizures, the shared phenotypes of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in ARX that lead to gain-of-function mechanisms in either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ARX in neuronal development provides a potential target for therapeutic interventions aimed at improving cognitive function and seizure control in patients with either disease.

#### 2. corpus callosum agenesis-abnormal genitalia syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.786)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:18060)

**Proposed mechanism:** ARX (HGNC:18060) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal genitalia (HP:0000027); ARX (HGNC:18060) —LEADS_TO→ Corpus callosum agenesis (HP:0001274); ARX (HGNC:18060) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Loss-of-function mutations in the ARX gene lead to both abnormal genitalia and corpus callosum agenesis, which are key features of intellectual disability syndromes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of individuals with pathogenic ARX variants who do not exhibit both abnormal genitalia and corpus callosum agenesis would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs115647804)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the role of ARX in both genital and brain development could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for congenital anomalies affecting these systems.
